revalidation_2026-07-28_294.method: 2026-07-28 revalidation for issue #294 (all 13 descriptions compressed to the amended section-3.5 200-400 char target): section-6.5 fan-out, one fresh-context sonnet (low effort) agent per query, each shown the full lettered menu of all 13 NEW descriptions (under-test skill unflagged, letter K) plus NONE, asked which ONE to load; one opus adjudicator per skill scored from reasoning per section-6.5 step 4. No fable-model agents. Conductor session: #294 worktree.

misses.query: convert this cuirass from slot 32 to slot 52 so it stops clipping with my body — edit the FirstPersonFlags on the record
misses.diagnosis: K's lead promise ("translate a slot number… into its BodyTemplate.FirstPersonFlags bit value") reads as the authoritative owner of the slot→bit datum, so a WRITE that needs that bit still routes to K; the "editing a record's own fields is skypatcher-authoring" boundary clause is outranked because the agent judged the bit lookup, not the write, to be the load-bearing step.

revalidation_2026-07-28_294.adjudicator_notes:
Recall 10/10, specificity 9/10 — passes both thresholds (>=0.80 / >=0.50) comfortably. No reasoning-vs-token overrides applied: every pick token matched its own reasoning.

Recall rows 1-10 are all clean, high-confidence matches; several cite K's description near-verbatim (slot 52/SOS, FirstPersonFlags→slot, \"which slot does this piece use\"), so the trigger clause is doing real work rather than the agent guessing from the skill name.

Specificity notes worth flagging even though they scored as hits:
- Row 15 (\"conceptual difference between FirstPersonFlags and BipedObjectFlags in xEdit\") is a near-miss: the agent deliberated at length, called K \"the only entry touching these exact fields at all,\" and only landed on N because K's trigger is task-shaped (\"find equippable on a slot\") rather than explanatory. That task-shaped framing is what saved the row — worth preserving if the description is ever revised.
- Row 14 (invisible SOS mesh) and row 17 (neck seam/wrist gap) both mention SOS/body-mod symptoms without K firing, so the \"SOS\"/\"pelvis\" keywords in K's description are not over-attracting on their own.
- Rows 12, 19, 20 all went to D (bulk-record-jobs) on \"find/list many records\" phrasing that lacks a slot term — the D vs K boundary is holding on the presence of an actual slot/flag concept.

Only structural weakness: the sole miss (row 18) is the find-vs-edit boundary. K already carries the disclaimer sentence (\"This finds and filters records BY slot — … editing a record's own fields is skypatcher-authoring\"), but it sits after the datum promise and does not cover the case where the edit target IS the FirstPersonFlags field itself. Arguably defensible as a soft miss — the slot→bit mapping genuinely is needed to set that field correctly — so this is a low-priority tightening, not a failure driver.
revalidation_2026-07-28_294.contamination_audit_2026-07-28: 2026-07-28 PR #295 review follow-up (contamination audit): the independent review found adjudicator notes quoting text that exists only in the PRE-compression descriptions. Forensics on the run journal established: (a) judges were shown the NEW menu (the loader agent's journaled return contains it verbatim); (b) 11 of 281 judge rows leaked OLD description text from the agents' own environment skill listing (the installed plugin) into their reasoning; (c) separately, some opus adjudicator notes confabulated 'verbatim quotes' from that same stale environment. All contaminated rows were re-judged with a hardened prompt (explicit stale-environment warning): 15/15 confirmed their original verdicts, except dialogue-authoring q19, whose recorded MISS was itself a contamination artifact and is overturned. Treat quoted description text in the run-1 adjudicator_notes above as unreliable where it does not appear in the shipped description; scores are pick-derived and were confirmed by the hardened re-run. Skill-specific: the run-1 note's quotes of 'BodyTemplate.FirstPersonFlags' and an 'editing a record's own fields' boundary clause appear in NO judge reasoning — pure adjudicator confabulation from the stale environment. Superseded anyway: see revalidation_2026-07-28_294_v2 (description reworded per review; fresh full run).

revalidation_2026-07-28_294_v2.adjudicator_notes: Perfect run: recall 10/10, specificity 10/10, no misses, no reasoning/pick conflicts requiring override. Every recall row's reasoning cites a genuine slot-lookup intent, so all K picks are real selections rather than token-only matches. Notable: row 10 (reverse lookup, FirstPersonFlags value -> slot) is covered only implicitly by "translate a slot number or label ... into its `FirstPersonFlags` bit" - the judge read the direction as reversible and still picked K, so it lands as a hit, but the description never states the reverse direction explicitly; rows 2 and 10 both depend on that inference. Row 18 is direct evidence the restored boundary clause is load-bearing: the judge quoted "editing those records is `skypatcher-authoring`" and routed a FirstPersonFlags EDIT away from K to B - the exact near-miss the reword targeted. Row 15 (conceptual First Person Flags vs Biped Object Flags) went to schema lookup rather than K, showing "for a `cross_plugin_query` filter" successfully scopes K to query composition rather than field explanation. No environment contamination: every quotation attributed to K appears verbatim in the supplied description block. Rows 11 and 14 quote or paraphrase other menu letters' descriptions (J's KID text), which is outside the K block but permitted - the constraint applies to K's text only.
